q: Does the review tint stay a colour-only wash at 1.11:1, or does it get a second, non-colour channel?
lede: The tint is the only mark this product draws, and as built it is quieter than the divider lines it sits between.

visual.name: auth.md — Live mode, left gutter
visual.note: The gutter bar is the proposed second channel; the wash inside the text stays as designed.
visual.caption: Where a non-colour channel would sit, outside the reading line.

stakes: If nobody registers the mark, every review number after it measures a screen the reader never saw.
state: §10 says changed spans carry `a light tint and nothing else` (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:247).
The prototype ships `.m1{background:var(--wash);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--wash) inset}`, so the shadow is the fill's own hex (docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:116).
Measured from the declared hexes, the wash is 1.111:1 on white, under the 1.24:1 hairline beside it (docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:13).
§22 already promises `the tint is never colour alone`, which a wash plus a same-colour shadow does not keep (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:540).
path: §16 read Tang et al. as saying provenance awareness improves validation and raises workload (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:408).
The plan answered the workload half by making the mark as quiet as it could be.
It never asked what quiet costs on the perception side, and no eye-tracking has been run on our screens (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:402).
tension: Quiet enough to ignore at rest and loud enough to be seen are the same dial when colour is the only channel.
The scheduled test asks what the tint means, so someone who never saw it still produces an answer (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:411).
Whether a text wash falls under SC 1.4.11 is contested; a margin mark makes the argument unnecessary.

evidence.title: How loud each mark is against its own background
evidence.note: Contrast ratios derived by me from the prototype's declared hexes (docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:13, :14, :16, :22) using the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula. The 3:1 line is the floor the plan's own PRD applies to borders that identify a control (docs/FRONTMATTER-PRD-v2-2026-08-29.md:3357). Whether a text-background wash falls under that rule is contested — the same PRD row says "do not raise decorative dividers" — so read the line as the standard the design is being argued against, not a settled verdict.
evidence.thresholdLabel: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 floor the PRD applies to an identifying boundary

evidence.title: What the plan says about the tint, in three places

options.label: Ship the colour-only wash and let the five-second test decide
options.what: Nothing changes; the mark stays a background wash with no second channel.
gains: Cheapest; nothing to build, redraw or re-test
Defensible if a document wash reads as decoration, not as a control boundary
costs: Someone who missed the tint still answers the meaning question
§22's colour-alone promise stays false

options.label: Add one gutter mark at 3:1 and keep the text wash quiet
options.what: A left-margin bar marks the span; the wash inside the text is unchanged.
gains: Keeps §22's promise and ends the SC 1.4.11 argument
Puts the mark in the left column §16 says is scanned first
One CodeMirror gutter decoration
costs: Gutter width is also wanted by line numbers and git marks
A second element to draw in every mode and both themes
options.system: One gutter decoration in the review-state layer; no sidecar or engine change.
options.screens: S2, S4, split and Read gain a gutter column.

options.label: Raise the wash itself to 3:1
options.what: The tint becomes a visible highlight behind the text.
gains: One token change and impossible to miss
costs: The document reads as highlighted, the exact failure the test exists to catch
Rejected by §16's own workload argument
options.screens: Every screen carrying the tint changes character.

options.label: Make the channel a setting: wash, wash plus gutter, or gutter only
options.what: The reader picks how the mark is drawn.
gains: Nobody has to be right first time
costs: Three states to design, test and screenshot
The promise rests on whichever is default, so the default is still this decision
options.system: A preference, plus the gutter work anyway.
options.screens: One more control on S11, which the wireframes want short.

recCase: §22 already commits to never colour alone, and a gutter mark is the cheapest way to keep that promise.
Tang's workload cost is about attention inside the text; a margin mark sits outside it.
The gutter also has room for the count, so this and D4 can share one column.
flip: If the rewritten noticing test in D18 finds people spot the wash unprompted at 1.111:1, the gutter mark is decoration.

q: Do we keep two washes for proposed and unreviewed, or does the bordered highlight already in the codebase become the proposal mark?
lede: One tint means the bytes are on your disk, the other means nothing was written, and only hue separates them.

visual.note: The two planned washes are 4.10 apart on delta-E76, against a just-noticeable difference near 2.3.
visual.caption: Three span treatments: two are drawn, one is already shipping.

stakes: Confusing the two states means reverting bytes that never changed, or accepting text believing it is already saved.
state: The wireframes are explicit: purple is proposed, blue is written but unreviewed (docs/_wireframes.md:29).
Both wash hexes are declared on one line and differ by delta-E76 4.10 (docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:14).
`.cm-ai-suggestion` is merged with a blue fill, a 1px inset border, 3px corners and a pulse (src/app/globals.css:833, :835, :836, :844).
The planned tint is unbuilt: no file in `src/` carries review-tint state.
path: F2 marks what an agent already wrote; F5 and F8 deliver text that has not been written (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:56, :59).
Both were given a tinted span because tinting is the product's one visual idiom.
`.cm-ai-suggestion` arrived with the sibling app's inline accept and reject, before §16's tint rules were written.
tension: The distinction with a data consequence is carried by the weakest channel available.
Working code already gives the proposal a border, which is the non-colour channel the distinction needs.
Keeping it breaks §16's `no border, no icon` rule for one of the two marks (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:408).
The pulse runs with `prefers-reduced-motion` absent from the whole stylesheet (docs/FRONTMATTER-PRD-v2-2026-08-29.md:3366).

items: derived by me from docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:14; JND is about 2.3

the two are indistinguishable by luminance; only hue separates them
Scheduled tests that show both states

rows: flips a flag, changes zero bytes (docs/_wireframes.md:29)

inset 1px at 30% over that fill → ≈#93b6fc, 1.53:1 against the fill and 1.95:1 against the page

items: Files in src/ carrying review-tint state

options.label: Keep both washes as drawn and delete the shipped highlight
options.what: One quiet idiom; the proposal is a purple wash with no border.
gains: One vocabulary, and §16's rules stay enforceable
Nothing on the page competes with the review tint
costs: The data-consequence distinction rests on a 4.1 delta-E hue difference
F8's inline accept and reject has to be redrawn
options.system: Delete `.cm-ai-suggestion` and its keyframes; build the proposal decoration.
options.screens: S3b and S4 keep their drawn treatment.

options.label: Adopt the shipped bordered highlight as the proposal mark, and correct the plan
options.what: Proposals are blue with a border, review state is the quiet wash, and the wireframes' purple goes.
gains: The difference survives greyscale, dark mode and colour-blindness
Reuses code that works, at close to no build cost
costs: The `no border` rule then applies to one mark only and must be written down
Two blue marks of different loudness in one editor
options.system: Keep the class, wrap the pulse in `prefers-reduced-motion`, rewrite the wireframe note.
options.screens: S3b and S4 redraw the proposal span.

options.label: Keep both washes and add a dashed left rule to the proposal
options.what: The purple stays and gains a non-colour mark of its own design.
gains: Keeps the drawn palette and makes the distinction non-hue
costs: Builds a second treatment when one is already merged
Adds an element to the surface §16 tried to keep clear

options.label: Take the proposal out of the document; it lives in the review panel
options.what: Nothing unwritten is ever tinted in the text.
gains: Removes the confusion by removing the second state from the page
One tint to test and one meaning to teach
costs: Forfeits proposal-arrives-in-place, which F5 and F8 were designed around
S3b answer-in-place is redrawn from scratch
options.system: Proposals render in the panel only.

recCase: A border is the second channel the distinction needs, and it is already merged and working.
Correcting a wireframe note costs less than rebuilding the same idea in a different colour.
The motion guard is due either way, since `prefers-reduced-motion` appears zero times in the stylesheet.
flip: If the inline accept and reject flow is being replaced by the review panel, delete the class and take option a.

q: Should the tint be switchable at all, and is it on by default?
lede: The settings page ships a toggle that turns off the one thing this product adds to a markdown editor.

visual.title: S11 Settings, as built

rows.label: Mark machine-written text until a person reviews it
Show the unreviewed bar in the file tree

visual.note: The settings copy already says the tint is file state, not AI.
visual.caption: Which switches remove chrome, and which remove the product.

stakes: A pilot participant who switches the tint off is counted as a user of a product they are not using.
state: S11 ships `Mark machine-written text until a person reviews it` and a tree-bar toggle, both on (docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:615, :616).
The hide-all-AI switch already draws the line: the review tint stays, because it is file state (docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:608).
The MVP-0 exit measure counts days opened, spans reviewed and proposals accepted (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:431).
path: The hide-all switch is evidence-backed: Zed, VS Code and Telegram shipped theirs after 412-, 30- and 181-reaction issues (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:298).
The tint toggle followed from the settings page's habit of making every visual behaviour optional.
tension: The wireframes state the rule being broken: every toggle we add is a decision we failed to make (docs/_wireframes.md:47).
With the tint off, 41 of 43 editor files are byte-identical to the sibling app, so nothing distinct is left (docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:223).
Removing a control that already works is the kind of change those three reaction counts were about.

evidence.title: Settings toggles on S11, counted
items: Of those, toggles that disable the product's core signal
:615 "Mark machine-written text…" and :616 "Show the unreviewed bar in the file tree"
"Every toggle we add is a decision we failed to make"
Editor files byte-identical to the sibling app
docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:223 — what is left when the tint is off
What the MVP-0 exit test counts
docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:431 — all three read zero for a user who switched the tint off

options.label: Keep both toggles, default on
options.what: Nothing changes; the reader can switch off the tint and the tree bar.
gains: Maximum control, and nobody can call the mark forced
costs: The exit measure reads zero for a user who switched it off
Two more states in every test and screenshot

options.label: Remove the tint toggle; keep the tree-bar toggle
options.what: The tint is not optional; the tree bar stays chrome that can be hidden.
gains: Two fewer states to design, test and support
The pilot measures one product
costs: A vocal user can reasonably object to a removed control
Someone who wants a clean document has only the file itself

options.label: Make the tint per-document, stored in frontmatter
options.what: A finished document can be marked as no longer needing marks.
gains: Matches the projection law: the setting lives in the file
A shipped document reads clean without a global switch
costs: A new frontmatter key to read, write and refuse on
SAFE_KEY governs what can be addressed there (src/modules/share/domain/splice-frontmatter.ts:53)
options.system: One key in the reader and writer, plus a refusal path.
options.screens: The properties panel gains a row.

options.label: Replace both with one quiet mode
options.what: A single switch dims every review signal at once.
gains: One decision instead of two, and an answer to reviewer fatigue
costs: Still ships an off switch for the product
A dimmed state has to be designed and measured too
options.screens: S11 loses a row; every surface gains a dimmed state.

recCase: The hide-all switch already says the right thing out loud: AI is optional, file state is not.
A second switch that contradicts it hands the pilot a way to be a non-user without leaving.
The tree bar is chrome and can stay optional at no cost to the exit measure.
flip: If a pilot participant asks for it unprompted the need is real, and option c is the right shape for it.
